note: Re-derived by hand from data/pages/singlesignon__latest__userguide__awsapps-that-work-with-identity-center.md, row by row, with python over the raw table, and independently of the parser's output. The table has 40 data rows and 5 columns. Column 1 is the AWS managed application; columns 2-5 are four different IAM Identity Center capabilities, so each is its own feature: account instances, trusted identity propagation, customer managed KMS key, and deployment in additional Regions. The axis is service in all four: the question each column answers is which applications, and therefore which AWS services, have the capability. Column 5 mentions Regions but names no Region, and no Region is counted. Every cell carries an icon image followed by the word Yes or No. Raw per-column word totals over the 40 rows: account instances 29 Yes / 11 No; trusted identity propagation 25 / 15; customer managed KMS key 37 / 3; additional Regions 14 / 26. On exactly six rows the icon contradicts the word, always in the customer managed KMS key column, always a negative icon next to the word Yes: Amazon EMR Serverless, Amazon Managed Grafana, Amazon Redshift, Amazon SageMaker Studio, Amazon WorkSpaces, AWS Deadline Cloud. The word is read, not the icon. Reason: the page's own note says applications that support deployment in additional Regions also support a customer managed KMS key, and three of the six (EMR Serverless, Redshift, Deadline Cloud) say Yes to additional Regions, so reading their icon would make the table contradict the rule the page states above it, while reading the word leaves all 14 additional-Regions rows consistent with it. The icon is also an image with empty alt text, which conveys nothing to a screen reader, so the word is the cell's only readable verdict. Reading the icon instead would give 28 covered services in that column rather than 33: emr-serverless, grafana, redshift, workspaces and deadline would drop out, while sagemaker stays because the Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio row carries a positive icon. Rows are application names, not always service names. Each label was resolved with resolveService; if that failed, the label without its trailing parenthetical and the parenthetical alone were tried (that recovers 'AWS account access (account access manager)' -> account-access); if that also failed, an explicit alias naming the owning service was tried: Amazon Athena SQL -> Amazon Athena (athena), Amazon EKS Capabilities -> Amazon EKS (eks), Amazon EMR on EC2 and Amazon EMR Studio -> Amazon EMR (elasticmapreduce), Amazon EMR on EKS -> Amazon EMR Containers (emr-containers, which is the IAM service for EMR on EKS - not elasticmapreduce), Amazon OpenSearch Service Serverless Service -> Amazon OpenSearch Serverless (aoss), Amazon S3 Access Grants -> Amazon S3 (s3), Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio -> Amazon SageMaker (sagemaker), AWS Transfer Family web apps -> AWS Transfer Family (transfer). Amazon EMR Serverless needs no alias: it resolves on its own to emr-serverless. Amazon Quick resolves to quicksight, which carries 'Amazon Quick' as a published name; the synthetic regional:amazon-quick row no longer makes it ambiguous. Two rows resolve to nothing and are recorded in unresolved, never counted: Kiro (no entry in services.json carries the name) and OpenSearch user interface (Dashboards) (no entry names it; services.json has an opensearch id but it carries no names). So 38 rows resolved onto 36 distinct service ids. Two ids are hit by more than one row and are counted once: elasticmapreduce (Amazon EMR on EC2 and Amazon EMR Studio, which carry the same Yes in all four columns, so nothing is in doubt) and sagemaker (Amazon SageMaker Studio and Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio, which disagree in the account instances column and the additional Regions column: Studio No, Unified Studio Yes). Where colliding rows disagree the id is counted as covered, because one row says Yes, and marked partial with a note naming both rows. Per column, covered + excluded is 36, and 36 + 2 merged + 2 unresolved = 40 rows, so no row is dropped: account instances 26 + 10; trusted identity propagation 21 + 15; customer managed KMS key 33 + 3; additional Regions 13 + 23. Partials: account instances redshift (footnote 2 carves out applications like Query Editor v2 that require permission sets) and sagemaker (row disagreement); additional Regions sagemaker (row disagreement) and ssm (the cell reads 'Yes - Fleet Manager Remote Desktop', so only that part of Systems Manager). Footnote 3 sits on a No cell (AWS account access, additional Regions), which is an exclusion, and footnote 1 sits on Kiro, which never resolves, so neither creates a partial. The six icon/word conflicts are not carve-outs and do not make an item partial; they are recorded in the item note and in the feature notes.
